title: introduce connection murmuration and soft-deny holdoff to reduce cascade restarts
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: During a recent regional flapping incident we observed rapid connection churn and aggressive circuit resets causing downstream cascade restarts and SLO violations. This change introduces a lightweight behavioral smoothing layer we call 'connection murmuration' and pairs it with a configurable 'soft-deny holdoff' timer. The goal is to make transient node-level perturbations absorbable without triggering global circuit flips or tenant-wide evictions.

What this PR does: Adds a connection murmuration admission controller that groups near-simultaneous connection failures into a single dampened event and applies a short, progressive holdoff instead of immediate circuit reset. It also introduces a soft-deny mode for overloaded nodes which returns a deterministic 429+Retry-After with a coordinated holdoff window to clients and upstream routing so requests can be gently diverted rather than forcibly ejected. A compact on-disk snapshot of murmuration state allows fast restore after restarts so the system doesn't immediately re-trigger the same churn.

Design summary: - Murmuration controller maintains ephemeral cohorts keyed by region/node/tenant with exponential cool-down (50ms base, capped at 3s) and jitter to avoid synchronized retries. - Soft-deny holdoff exposes two knobs: holdoff_base_ms and holdoff_decay_factor. Holdoff is applied per-tenant on a node when local error rates exceed a configured SLO threshold for the node. - State persistence: a compact snapshot file persisted every 5s and on graceful shutdown. Snapshots are guarded by schema version to permit future upgrades. - Observability: new metrics (murmuration_cohort_count, murmuration_cohort_duration_ms, soft_deny_engagements_total) and structured logs when cohorts form or dissolve. - Safety: default config is opt-in (disabled in main) and toggled via runtime feature flag. Non-opted clusters see no semantic change.

Compatibility and rollout: The feature is implemented behind a runtime feature flag and controlled by the console rollout system. We recommend a staged rollout: Canary (internal test tenants) -> Regional (single low-traffic region) -> Global. Rollout includes phased enabling of snapshot-restores to avoid state amplification.

Testing and verification: - Unit tests for cohort lifecycle and holdoff math. - Integration test simulating a 30% spike in connection failures to ensure no more than 10% additional circuit resets vs baseline. - Local soak runs showing reduced SLO breaches under synthetic jittered failures. - Benchmarked overhead: median 0.4ms addition per admission under 95th-percentile load.

Checklist: - [x] Feature implemented behind flag - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests with failure injection harness - [x] Metrics and logging - [x] Console flag + rollout plan entry - [x] Docs stub added to operations handbook

Related tickets: Linear ENG-3421, ENG-3492.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps cohort keying conservative to avoid per-request allocations under high QPS. The core algorithm is lock-free for the hot path and uses sharded, time-windowed counters to approximate cohort windows.
commits: a1b2c3d: initial murmuration controller and tests
d4e5f6a: add soft-deny holdoff math and integration test harness
b7c8d9e: persist murmuration snapshots and add restore path
f0e1d2c: metrics/logging and console feature flag integration

review_comments: Ethan Chen: Overall design looks good. Two asks: (1) please ensure the snapshot format version is validated on load and log a warning rather than hard-failing for older snapshots; (2) add a test for the jitter distribution to avoid pathological alignment.
Maya Patel: Added snapshot schema validation and a warning path. Also added a jitter unit test that asserts expected spread across 10k samples; results included in test. PTAL.
Luis Ortega: Can we have an opt-out annotation per-tenant (operator override) in addition to console flag? Some enterprise customers want explicit tenant-level opt-out.
Maya Patel: Added tenant metadata override via tenant config and documented in ops page. Default is inherit-from-cluster to keep behavior predictable.
Ravi Singh: Integration tests flaked once on CI (integration/failure-injector). Reran and green. Consider increasing retry sleep on that harness to be less brittle.
Maya Patel: Increased harness stability and left a comment explaining conditions; integration tests are stable after change.
release_notes: Introduce an opt-in 'connection murmuration' admission controller and a configurable 'soft-deny holdoff' to reduce cascade restarts and smooth transient failure spikes. Disabled by default; enable via runtime feature flag and console rollout.
notes_for_ops: Enable behind feature flag. Recommended staged rollout: canary -> single region -> global. Snapshot restore can be enabled after at least 1 min of stable canary traffic to avoid replay of short-lived cohorts.
backout_plan: Disable feature flag and restart controlplane; snapshot file is ignored when flag is off so state won't be read. If issues persist, toggle tenant-level opt-out.
changelog_entry: features: connection murmuration & soft-deny holdoff (opt-in behind flag)
